explanation: The E138K substitution introduces a bulkier, positively charged residue that disrupts the electrostatic environment of the allosteric NNRTI-binding pocket despite not directly contacting nevirapine. The ~30 Ų volume expansion and charge reversal from negative to positive at position 138 in the connection subdomain likely propagates conformational strain through the flexible architecture linking this region to the NNRTI-binding site, destabilizing the precise geometry required for optimal nevirapine accommodation at the 11.9 Å interface. This indirect mechanism—altering the entropic penalty and backbone positioning of the binding pocket through electrostatic and steric perturbation of a distal but structurally coupled region—accounts for the modest but measurable loss of binding affinity without requiring direct ligand-mutation contacts.
